title: Naval on happiness, freedom and decisions: 44 truths about the game of life
summary: Naval argues success and happiness are not a trade-off: win the material game, then be free of it. He pushes holistic selfishness, scheduling freedom, productizing yourself, fast iteration with decisive exits, and picking who you're with, what you do and where you live deliberately. Business content is thin; mostly mindset and decision rules.

principles.text: Productize yourself: find what feels like play to you but looks like work to others.
principles.quote: find what feels like play to you but looks like work to others.

principles.text: Prefer wealth games over status games: wealth is positive sum, status is limited and combative.
principles.quote: wealth creation is positive but status is limited. There's limited status to go around. It's a ranking ladder.

principles.text: Get rich first, then pursue fame; building a following to get rich is the harder path.
principles.quote: that's a much harder path than getting rich first. Um and then go for your fame afterwards would be my advice.

principles.text: Explore broadly, then commit; the biggest mistake with many choices is premature commitment.
principles.quote: The biggest mistake in a world with so many choices is premature commitment.

principles.text: Mastery comes from iterations (error corrections), not repetitions; bail out fast when it isn't working.
principles.quote: Iteration is modifying it with a learning and then doing another version of it. So that's error correction.

principles.text: Decision heuristics: if you can't decide, say no; choose the shorter-term painful option; choose what leaves you calmer long term.
principles.quote: if you can't decide, the answer is no.
